author: Kyle Powell
title: Tage leads the way in crazy tilt at Anaheim - NewsBreak
text:
By Kyle Powell ,
2 hours ago
ANAHEIM, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 29: Tage Thompson #72 of the Buffalo Sabres reacts after scoring a goal during the first period of a game against the Anaheim Ducks at Honda Center on October 29, 2026 in Anaheim, California. (Photo by Sean M. Haffey/Getty Images)
Anaheim, California (WGR 550) - Take any preconceived notions you had about this game and throw them out the window. Visiting the Anaheim Ducks, the Buffalo Sabres erased a 3-1 deficit with six-unanswered goals. Each and every goal along the way was as important as the last, as the Ducks battled back to make it 7-6 before the curtain dropped on an unbelievable Sabres victory at the Honda Center.
There was no shortage of action in the first period, as the goals came not only early, but often.
Anaheim jumped out of the gates with two powerplay goals before three-minutes of game time had even expired. With former Duck Olen Zellweger and Zach Benson both in the penalty box, the home side bookended the 5-on-3 powerplay with goals from forwards Mikael Granlund and Cutter Gauthier.
The Sabres responded at the halfway point of the opening stanza. It was Tyson Kozak halving the deficit, as he made it 2-1 from downtown by using Beck Malenstyn as a screen in front of goalie Ville Husso.
Buffalo's one-goal deficit lasted all of 35-seconds, though. Ducks rookie forward Roger McQueen potted the first goal of his NHL career at the other end of the rink, as he solved Colten Ellis for the third time in 10:38 to make it 3-1 Anaheim.
Rather than stop at getting within a goal again, the Sabres posted the final two goals of a wild first period at Honda Center. Getting the job done first was Noah Ostlund, whose nifty powerplay goal was his fourth score of the season.
Following things up was the big fella. With 4:28 left in the frame, Tage Thompson showcased the talents that has made him a three-time 40-goal scorer in the NHL. Thompson accepted a pass from Benson, blew past the Anaheim defense, and with a strong power move beat Husso short-side for his sixth goal of 2026-27.
Turns out, that goal was just the beginning of another magical night for Thompson. After both teams were stymied for the first 18:36 of the second period, Tage turned one goal into a hat-trick in a matter of just 15-seconds!
Thompson's second came right off an offensive-zone face-off win. In the process, he took over the team-lead in goals from Jack Quinn with his seventh.
Shortly thereafter, Rasmus Dahlin exited the defensive zone by locating Thompson streaking up the right-wing side. He turned on the jets, and beat Husso five-hole for his 10th-career hat-trick.
The blue and gold barrage continued as the third period began in Anaheim. What was once a 3-1 deficit quickly turned into a 7-3 lead by the 6:37 mark of the final regulation frame. Scoring Buffalo's fifth and sixth unanswered goals, respectively, was the duo of Quinn and Benson. Quinn's was on the Sabres' second fruitful powerplay of the contest, while Benson cashed in on a breakaway for his second goal in as many games.
Less than a minute after Benson's goal, the Ducks finally put a stop to the Buffalo goal-scoring when Gauthier made it 7-4 Sabres. It was Gauthier's second goal of the night; both of the powerplay variety.
Amazingly, Anaheim made a real game of it before the final horn sounded. Very late goals from Tristan Luneau and Beckett Sennecke had the Honda Center on its feet, but despite the comeback time was not a friend of the Ducks. Sennecke's goal made it a 7-6 contest with just 31-seconds to play. Ellis hunkered down and made one more high-danger save, before an Anaheim icing with two-seconds to play all but sealed things in what was a "see it to believe it" kind of night in Orange County.

First Period:
BUF: 10:03 - Tyson Kozak (1) (Sam Carrick, Mattias Samuelsson); 11:39 - Noah Ostlund (4) PPG (Zach Benson, Tage Thompson); 15:31 - Tage Thompson (6) (Zach Benson, Peyton Krebs)
ANA: 1:57 - Mikael Granlund (3) PPG (Jackson LaCombe, Leo Carlsson); 2:54 - Cutter Gauthier (3) PPG (Beckett Sennecke, Leo Carlsson); 10:38 - Roger McQueen (1) (Sam Colangelo, Nick Jensen)
Second Period:
BUF: 18:36 - Tage Thompson (7) (Peyton Krebs); 18:51 - Tage Thompson (8) (Rasmus Dahlin, Peyton Krebs)
ANA: NONE
Third Period:
BUF: 1:57 - Jack Quinn (7) PPG (Tage Thompson, Rasmus Dahlin); 6:37 - Zach Benson (2) (Olen Zellweger)
ANA : 7:26 - Cutter Gauthier (4) PPG (Jackson LaCombe, Leo Carlsson); 18:52 - Tristan Luneau (2) (Judd Caufield); 19:29 - Beckett Sennecke (8) (Unassisted)
STATS OF THE GAME
Bluestar Home Services Three Stars of the Game:
1.) Tage Thompson - BUF
2.) Cutter Gauthier - ANA
3.) Peyton Krebs - BUF
